## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Piṇḍola Sutta* (Ud 4.6, PTS Ud 42) is the sixth discourse of the fourth chapter (*Meghiyavagga*) of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The sutta depicts the venerable elder Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja seated in meditation, providing the narrative setting for an inspired utterance (*udāna*) by the Buddha [SuttaCentral]. While modern scholarly literature frequently examines Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja's role in the Vinaya, his reputation in narrative literature, and the subsequent cult devoted to him across East Asia, none of the retrieved secondary literature focuses specifically on this brief discourse.
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels—chiefly corresponding to the verse—are found in verse collections and other canonical discourses, including *Dhammapada* verse 185, the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), the Chinese *Dharmapada* and *Udānavarga* collections (T 210.22, T 212.32, T 213.31), as well as Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 31 *Cittavarga* and Uv Kg 31) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse between Ud 4.6 and several other discourses in the *Udāna* featuring meditating disciples—most prominently the *Kaccāna Sutta* (Ud 7.8), *Mahāmoggallāna Sutta* (Ud 3.5), *Kaṅkhārevata Sutta* (Ud 5.7), *Subhūti Sutta* (Ud 6.7), *Cūḷapanthaka Sutta* (Ud 5.10), and *Sāriputtaupasama Sutta* (Ud 4.10) [DharmaNexus]. Further phraseological reuse is identified with sections of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 6) and several saṁyuttas of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 7, SN 16, SN 21, and SN 54), as well as the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches scoring at or above 10 [DharmaNexus].
